div.head: VII Atr 1.3
div.ab: Et omnis qui familiam habet efficiat, ut omnis hyremannus suus det unum denarium. Qui si non habeat, det dominus eius pro eo; et omnis tainus decimet totum quicquid habet.
Et omnis qui familiam habet efficiat, ut omnis hyremannus suus det unum denarium. Qui si non habeat, det dominus eius pro eo; et omnis tainus decimet totum quicquid habet.
Et omnis qui familiam habet efficiat, ut omnis hyremannus suus det unum denarium. Qui si non habeat, det dominus eius pro eo; et omnis tainus decimet totum quicquid habeat.

Und jeder der einen Haushalt [mit Gesinde] hat, bewirke, dass jeder seiner [Haushalts-]Untergebenen 1 Pfennig gebe. Wenn dieser [so viel] nicht besitzt, zahle sein Herr für ihn; und jeder Thegn verzehnte alles, was er besitzt.

And let everyone who has a household [with servants] see to it that each of his [household] dependants gives 1 penny. If he does not have [that much], let his lord pay for him; and let every thegn pay a tithe of all that he owns.

And everyone who has a household shall see to it that each of his dependents gives a penny. If anyone is without money, his lord shall give it for him; and every thegn shall render a tithe of all that he has.

And everyone who has a household is to ensure that each of those under him gives one penny. If anyone does not have it, the lord is to give it for him; and every thane is to give one-tenth of all he has.
div.note: those under him: The Old English term here is hyremann, which literally translates to “one who hears” or “one who obeys.” Interestingly, the (presumably) Norman translator of 7 Æthelred into Latin keeps this word and, below, witam (“penalty,” clause 7) in Old English, though with Latin declensions.

note.seg: Original las hiered; vgl. Gl Gefolge 20a; Haushalt 1
The original read hiered; cf. Gl Gefolge 20a; Haushalt 1

Wahrscheinlich ist Q zu bessern nach hiredmanna gehwilc VIIa 5 und I Atr 1, 10. Denn hyreman würde auch den Eingesessenen mit bezeichnen, der Land besitzen kann, also schon deshalb selbst steuerpflichtig wäre. Hier scheint der Landlose unter Kopfsteuer gestellt; s. 1, 2³

Q should probably be corrected after hiredmanna gehwilc VIIa 5 and I Atr 1, 10. For hyreman would also denote the settled inhabitant, who can own land and would therefore for that reason alone be liable to tax himself. Here it seems to be the landless man who is made subject to poll-tax; see 1, 2³

Dafür heafodman VIIa 5; vgl. die Glosse primas: heafodman vel thegn bei Ælfric. Thegn steht hier als Grundbesitzer über dem Bauern. Der Homilet verwässert dies, in Hinblick auf künftige Notfälle: hwilum be (mannes) teoðunge 171 (= 173)

Instead of this, heafodman VIIa 5; cf. the gloss primas: heafodman vel thegn in Ælfric. Thegn stands here as landowner above the peasant. The homilist waters this down with a view to future emergencies: hwilum be (mannes) teoðunge 171 (= 173)

Cf. the A.S. version, cap. 5, which suggests that the reading hyremannus has been wrongly substituted for hiredmannus, i.e. every member of his household. hyremannus would include dependents with houses and holdings who would be personally responsible for their dues.
